newsitem.title: FRANCE: France reassures Poland on its EU membership bid.
newsitem.headline: France reassures Poland on its EU membership bid.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac assured Polish Prime Minister Wladimir Cimoszewicz on Wednesday of his continued strong support for Polish membership of the European Union as early as the year 2000, a Chirac aide said.

Cimoszewicz, for his part, expressed the hope that NATO would begin negotiations, following its July summit in Madrid, on bringing Warsaw into the Atlantic alliance, Chirac spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told reporters after the two leaders met.

The two agreed that an acceptable role for Russia in Europe's security architecture was crucial to NATO expansion, and that this challenge must be addressed as part of the preparations for the Madrid meeting, Colonna said.

Cimoszewicz had said ahead of his visit to Paris, which began on Wednesday, that he sought new assurances that the NATO summit would make concrete decisions on the start of talks with Poland and that negotiations would start in 1998 on EU enlargement into central and eastern Europe.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt recalled that Chirac had previously expressed strong support for Poland's admission to NATO during a visit to Warsaw last September.
Rummelhardt said Franco-Polish trade exchanges were booming, with a 47 percent increase last year, making France the third largest investor in Poland and its fourth largest trading partner.

Cimoszewicz said he wanted French business to be even more active in Poland. He also hoped France would help expand the teaching of the French language to compete with successful British and U.S. campaigns to push the English language.
France has launched an all-out drive to court Eastern Europe. Chirac, who visited Hungary recently, is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Sunday and visit Romania next month.
The presidents of Ukraine, Romania, Georgia and Estonia are all due to visit Paris in the next few days.
